questions.stem: What are the two main parts of the central nervous system (CNS)?

options.text: The spinal cord and peripheral nerves

questions.explanation: The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord. The brain is the main coordination centre, while the spinal cord connects the brain to the peripheral nervous system and coordinates reflexes.

questions.stem: Which type of neurone carries impulses FROM the CNS to effectors?
questions.explanation: Motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS (brain or spinal cord) to effectors (muscles or glands). Sensory neurones carry impulses in the opposite direction, from receptors to the CNS.

questions.stem: What is the correct order of information flow through the nervous system?
questions.explanation: Information flows from receptors (which detect stimuli) to the CNS (which processes the information and decides on a response) to effectors (muscles or glands that carry out the response).

questions.stem: Which division of the autonomic nervous system is responsible for 'fight or flight' responses?
questions.explanation: The sympathetic division of the autonomic nervous system controls 'fight or flight' responses, such as increasing heart rate and dilating pupils. The parasympathetic division controls 'rest and digest' responses.

questions.stem: How does the nervous system differ from the endocrine system in its response speed?

options.text: Both systems respond at the same speed
The nervous system only responds to internal stimuli
The nervous system produces faster, shorter-lived responses
The nervous system produces slower, longer-lasting responses

questions.explanation: The nervous system uses electrical impulses that travel very quickly, producing fast but short-lived responses. The endocrine system uses hormones transported in the blood, which is slower but produces longer-lasting effects.
Relay neurones (also called interneurones) are found within the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord). They connect sensory neurones to motor neurones and help process information.

questions.stem: What is the role of the peripheral nervous system?

options.text: To produce hormones for long-term control
To connect the CNS to the rest of the body
To process and interpret sensory information
To store memories and coordinate thought

questions.explanation: The peripheral nervous system (PNS) connects the central nervous system to the rest of the body. It contains sensory neurones that carry impulses to the CNS and motor neurones that carry impulses from the CNS to effectors.
